acceptance_criteria: Scope determination made (in-scope or out-of-scope) with reasoning

scope_determination.reasoning: scripts/seed_swiftroute_definition.sh is a bash deployment helper. It does not add or modify any file in lib/letflow/, priv/repo/migrations/, config/, or any Elixir source. The five scope-test triggers are all negative: (1) no new API route added; (2) no tenant data isolation change in Elixir; (3) no new authorization rules or bypass of existing ones; (4) no migration touching a business table; (5) no secret resolution in Elixir code.

hardcoded_secrets.detail: All credential material is sourced exclusively from environment variables. The script explicitly checks `if [[ -z "${QA_AUTH_TOKEN:-}" ]]` and exits 1 if unset. No token literal appears anywhere in the file.

authorization_bypass.detail: The script calls only the standard public API endpoints (/api/v1/definitions, /api/v1/definitions/{id}/activate) with a bearer token supplied via QA_AUTH_TOKEN. No backdoor, admin bypass, or undocumented endpoint is used.

token_sourcing.detail: Bearer token read from environment (${QA_AUTH_TOKEN}) at the point of use; never threaded through a struct, log call, or intermediate variable beyond AUTH_HEADER. The token itself is never echoed to stdout.

error_handling.detail: set -euo pipefail is set at the top of the script. Each curl call has an explicit `|| { echo ERROR; exit 1; }` guard. The script fails closed: any HTTP error aborts with a non-zero exit code and a diagnostic message to stderr.
